Previously when we had this issue, it was because of an older xml used.Process followed on WWIP end for crime score analysis:Verify the location address with google – in WWIP UI Location panel .Send this address to VRISKIf VRISK return the response – we display Crime score as is no conversation .If VRISK do not retrun the response or error out – we display 0 as crime score and when evenr next time user try to to rate we retry VRSIK in indication module or during the Endorsement module.During the renewal time – we call alternate year instead of every year call to VRISK. Both WWIP and Palantir uses Verisk end point with CAP current index value to report the numbers.Product is responsible to provide the users with the latest XML.Crime scores can change over time, as the underlying data is continuously being updatedAdditional notes from Verisk:From Verisk’s perspective, I would like to share that Crime scores are more likely to fluctuate than other LOCATION products. There are many underlying data inputs for Crime that are continuously updated (as opposed to other LOCATION products that are only updated monthly or quarterly), meaning that a score could change for a single address at any time.  Crime scores are also scaled with greater granularity than many other LOCATION products, so slight alternations to underlying data can cause perceivable differences.Also, just in case you may have access to both, I wanted to remind you that the Crime algorithms for Personal lines and Commercial lines are different – so the scores will differ and are not meant to match.Additionally, LOCATION is designed to return valid single addresses – not address ranges, nor aliases.  Even though aliases are recognized within our database, inputting them both at the same time could trigger matching issues.

Notes: 2/28 - Timo - Deployed last week.  2/25 - Timo We made a further analysis into what happened, and the fallback branch was not the root cause. As part of normal development practice, a configuration change was performed on one of the development branches. After performing the action, the platform frontend indicated that the change had not gone through properly, which prompted the developer to perform the action again. The second action affected the master branch which is what caused the disruption to production. As a remediation, we raised a ticket with our Product Team to disallow the conditions under which the second action was performed. They root caused and promptly resolved the issue today. Additionally, I want to clarify that fallback branches are solely used to ensure builds can fallback to data from another branch during development. Fallback branches are read-only and any change on a branch does not interfere with its fallback branches.  Issue Summary:Prod submissions were getting stuck in the ingestion process due to transaction IDs not being assigned to the submissions. Root cause:The issue occurred because the fallback configuration for a transform (all_text_extracted) build was incorrectly set to master branch by default. Master is always the default setting for all branches and this has never been changed.As a result, in an edge case where a development branch required a specific configuration change, unintended interference occurred. This misconfiguration led to transaction IDs not being assigned properly. Impact:5 submissions were not processed as expected, leading to the ingestion failures. Corrective actions:The fallback configuration was corrected to ensure it does not default to the master branch inappropriately.A review configuration process is being conducted for all branches to prevent similar issues in the future.We are working on setting up the monitoring for all status (currently only available for Classification) by 2/28 and we will expose it to the prod support team.  Note:A fallback branch is necessary to ensure that builds and deployment can proceed smoothly, even when the intended branch is unavailable. This allows ensuring build continuity, preventing misconfiguration.
Root Cause: Root cause:The issue occurred because the fallback configuration for a transform (all_text_extracted) build was incorrectly set to master branch by default. Corrective and Preventive Action Taken: As the network issue is rare to occur across the retry, we do not recommend an immediate hotpatch. Nevertheless, we should continue to monitor for this. To remedy this issue long-term, we can increase the number of retries and/or add an additional error when the CM cannot return a document due to a network blip. But there is a business question whether the failure to download a subset of documents should halt submission ingestion as a whole.The standard approach in such cases will be the missing/impacted fields to be updated via HITL edits and moved forward.

Root Cause: Below is the RCA for the prod defect where a submission downloaded only received 5 out of 10 documents from GDMS. The issue resulted from a rare and brief network blip during document download from GDMS by the CM for those five documents despite a retry in the CM. The function that calls the CM (createDocuments) iterates over the documents returned by the CM to add them to the submission. But the CM could not include the documents due to the network failure, so from the perspective of createDocuments, it was treated as if the documents did not exist and the submission continued processing. The network issue was so brief that only those five of ten documents were impacted.

Name: [Prod Issue] Influx of Emails sent as submissions for PNP Renewal
Description: Issue:Influx of Emails sent as submissions for LexMM and PNP Renewal
Notes: Below is the update from the team for high inflow of LEXMM Submissions.Issue: Influx of Emails sent as submissions for Lex MM Casualty and Property (1.5k emails in 3 hours) RCA: The WWIP application provides an email capability for underwriters to communicate with Brokers. This email correspondence is sent to the same ImageRight email receiver as the submission emails from external brokers. The ImageRight event hub sends an event to UW Assist for every email ingested by this receiver. This results in all the internal correspondence emails triggering a ‘new submission’ event to UW Assist and these emails getting extracted as submissions downstream. Impact: The impact on the users is not significant. The SSC users will see the emails that are not submissions also appear as submissions in their UWA display but this does not impact their reservation process. The correspondence emails go to a different queue in ImageRight and not in the submissions queue. The SSC users only look at the submissions queue and search for each submission in the IR queue by entering the IR ID in UWA submissions screen. Hence only the corresponding submission will be matched in UWA and reserved. There is an impact in terms of the data and potentially performance (though no performance issues seen so far), as all the correspondence emails are extracted and stored as submissions. Solution: The ImageRight workflows that process the ingested emails in the IR receiver need to be updated, to not create an event for UWA if the email originates from a ‘aig.com’ email. This will require a development and testing effort estimated to be 2-3 days. The ETA for deploying the fix to production is 11/7 (Friday)  Below is the update from the team for high inflow of QUIC Renewal Submissions. Issue: Influx of Emails sent as submissions for FL PNP (~8000 renewals accounts processed by UWA Batch jobs and sent to BE team11/03) RCA: The Renewal records processed and sent to BE team on 11/03 contained Primary, Excess, and non UWA FL PNP accounts. Processing Excess accounts is planned in the next release (Tentative 1.9). However, the DB scripts containing excess scope was merged in the 10/31 release by error which caused the job to pick up additional accounts for BE processing. Solution: QUIC team fixed the job by excluding the excess script and provided the Primary accounts to BE team for processing. This will address the accounts processed today and go forward the job will pick up only Primary accounts. No impact to Business Users as the data was not processed from the backend. Preventive measure: Established code review controls for all UWA QUIC changes in place to make sure this doesn’t happen again. QUIC team will work on the impact analysis for the non UWA FL PNP renewal accounts and closely work with BE team.
Root Cause: Issue: Influx of Emails sent as submissions for Lex MM Casualty and Property (1.5k emails in 3 hours)RCA: The WWIP application provides an email capability for underwriters to communicate with Brokers. This email correspondence is sent to the same ImageRight email receiver as the submission emails from external brokers. The ImageRight event hub sends an event to UW Assist for every email ingested by this receiver. This results in all the internal correspondence emails triggering a ‘new submission’ event to UW Assist and these emails getting extracted as submissions downstream. Issue: Influx of Emails sent as submissions for FL PNP (~8000 renewals accounts processed by UWA Batch jobs and sent to BE team11/03)RCA: The Renewal records processed and sent to BE team on 11/03 contained Primary, Excess, and non UWA FL PNP accounts. Processing Excess accounts is planned in the next release (Tentative 1.9). However, the DB scripts containing excess scope was merged in the 10/31 release by error which caused the job to pick up additional accounts for BE processing.

Name: [Prod Issue] [LexPro] LexPro Cyber / E&O Status Not Updating
Corrective and Preventive Action Taken: Hi team,The below issue is due to a duplicate coverages issue - mismatch between QUIC and UWA, specifically ‘MEDIA’ coverages. In UWA, we have ‘MEDIA’ as a single coverage, and in QUIC, shared services has the option to select any of 4 different coverages that are ‘MEDIA’ coverages.
